exposure: Mode of birth (vaginal vs. primary cesarean section)
outcome: Accuracy of methods in determining neutrophil composition
cohort: The study included 10 adult controls and 38 neonates (21 delivered vaginally, 17 by primary cesarean section).
finding: Flow cytometry was superior to manual differentials in identifying the earliest neutrophil forms and showed significant differences in neutrophil composition between newborns and adults that MDs did not.
mod_finding: Neonates showed similar neutrophil composition findings irrespective of labor and method of birth.
cross-section timing: Samples were obtained via cord blood from neonates at birth and by venipuncture in adults at a single time point.
